options.content: UTM - UCS Traffic Monitoring

panels.description:
Traffic monitoring of a server and related entities like vNIC/vHBA, backplane ports, etc.
 -  Search a *Service Profile* from the drop-down menu at the top of the page.
 -  Use the *UCS Domain* drop down menu to limit the scope to a specific UCS domain or select *All* to search from all the available service profiles.
Displayed color (Green or Orange) based on the operational state of the service profile

panels.description:
**Use Case**: Find traffic utilization and top talkers on backplane ports (between IOM/FEX and server)

![Backplane port traffic](/public/img/utm/backplane_port_traffic_per_vif.png)

**How to use**: Look for overutilization of backplane ports. Also, find the busiest/top-talker vNIC/vHBA on that backplane port.

**Details**: 
 - Over-utilized backplane port may lead to packet drop for Ethernet traffic or PAUSE frame activity for FC traffic (non-drop class) leading to congestion. Also, look under Congestion monitoring to monitor PAUSE frames for FC traffic.
 - These graphs are not generated if your servers are directed to connected to the FI. In that case, the FI ports are still called Server Ports, not backplane Ports. Go to Domain Traffic dashboard to monitor FI Server Ports.

targets.query: SELECT max("bytes_rx_delta")  / [[polling_interval]]*8 AS "RX" FROM "$db"."$rp"."VnicStats" WHERE ("service_profile" =~ /^$service_profile$/ AND "vif_name" =~ /^$vif$/ AND "peer_port" =~ /^$bp_port$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "vif_name"

SELECT max("bytes_tx_delta") *8 / [[polling_interval]] AS "TX" FROM "$db"."$rp"."BackplanePortStats" WHERE ("peer_service_profile" =~ /^$service_profile$/ AND "bp_port" =~ /^$bp_port$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "bp_port"

SELECT max("speed")  *1000000000 AS "TX Util Max" FROM "$db"."$rp"."BackplanePortStats" WHERE ("peer_service_profile" =~ /^$service_profile$/ AND "bp_port" =~ /^$bp_port$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "bp_port"

SELECT last("speed")  /last("speed") AS "TX % Max" FROM "$db"."$rp"."BackplanePortStats" WHERE ("peer_service_profile" =~ /^$service_profile$/ AND "bp_port" =~ /^$bp_port$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "bp_port"

SELECT max("bytes_tx_delta")  *8/[[polling_interval]]/max("speed")/1000000000 AS "TX % Util" FROM "$db"."$rp"."BackplanePortStats" WHERE ("peer_service_profile" =~ /^$service_profile$/ AND "bp_port" =~ /^$bp_port$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "bp_port"

panels.description:
**Use Case**: Find traffic congestion on backplane ports (between IOM/FEX and server)
![Backplane port ingress congestion](/public/img/utm/backplane_port_rx_pause.png)

**How to use**: A (sustained) spike in PAUSE frame rate is a good indication of congestion. An increase in traffic rate at the same time is a very strong evidence of congestion and also signals that congestion is due to over-utilization.

**Details**: 
 - The graphs show PAUSE frame and traffic rate on backplane ports which connect blade servers and IOM within a UCS chassis.
 - PAUSE frames are sent by a traffic receiver when it is unable to receive the traffic at the incoming rate.
 - On a port, RX traffic should be compared againt TX PAUSE and vice-versa.
 - Focus on (sustained) spikes only because PAUSE frames may be exchanged under normal condition also.
 - PAUSE frames are not reported at a per vNIC/vHBA level.

panels.description:
**Use Case**: Find traffic congestion on backplane ports (between IOM and blade server)
![Backplane port ingress congestion](/public/img/utm/backplane_port_tx_pause.png)

**How to use**: A sustained spike in PAUSE frame rate is a good indication of congestion. Increase in traffic rate at the same time is a very strong evidence of congestion and also signals that congestion is due to over-utilization.

**Details**: 
 - The graphs show PAUSE frame and traffic rate on backplane ports which connect blade servers and IOM within a UCS chassis.
 - PAUSE frames are sent by a traffic receiver when it is unable to receive the traffic at the incoming rate.
 - On a port, RX traffic should be compared againt TX PAUSE and vice-versa.
 - Focus on (sustained) spikes only because PAUSE frames may be exchanged under normal condition also.
 - PAUSE frames are not reported at a per vNIC/vHBA level.

panels.description:
**Use Case**: Verify (uniform) traffic distribution over FI-A and FI-B.

**How to use**: Give a quick look to the graph on the left and the graph on the right. If they look similar, traffic distribution is uniform.

**Details**: Inbound and Outbound traffic over FI-A and FI-B is shown side-by-side with the granularity of traffic type (FC/Ethernet) and vNIC/vHBA.
